5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtCoverBridge
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OverSigmaExtension
8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability
9	
10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	
44	universe u
45	
46	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

77	/-- **A chart family whose chart parameter varies with the index.**
78	
79	Each index `i` carries its own degree parameter `nn i`, its own representing object `D i` of
80	`divFunctor C π (nn i)`, its own twist exponent `m i` and chart index `Z i` — the latter legal
81	*at `nn i`*, i.e. `deg_k (Z i) = (m i)·d₁ − nn i`, which is what `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup`
82	requires for that index's chart value to land in `pic⁰`.
83	
84	The construction is just `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise; the content is
85	that it *typechecks*, i.e. that the target `pic0SigmaSheaf C` is parameter-free. -/
86	def mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)

92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
95	
96	variable (C π) in

98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :

112	  huniv i

116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine

124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/

130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))

8	/-!
9	# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
12	is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
13	of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
14	verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
15	index per point of `T`".
16	
17	**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
18	produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
19	chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
20	membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
21	`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
22	connection is what this file supplies.
23	
24	## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline
25	
26	Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:
27	
28	* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
29	  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
30	  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
31	  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
32	* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
33	  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
34	  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
35	  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
36	* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
37	  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
38	  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
39	  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
44	  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
45	  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
47	  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
48	  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise` — the composite: pointwise
50	  coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, i.e.
51	  B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the **converse**, and the reason this
53	  is a reduction rather than a restatement: the sieve condition gives back an open cover of
54	  the test on each of whose members some chart hits `s`.  So the pointwise form is not a
55	  strengthening chosen to be provable.
56	-/
57	
58	set_option autoImplicit false
59	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

61	universe u
62	
63	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
64	
65	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
66	
67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
68	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
69	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
70	
71	noncomputable section
72	
73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
74	
75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
78	
79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
80	
81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
84	
85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
88	
89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
101	
102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
103	
104	variable (C) in
105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
106	
107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
110	
111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
119	
120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
123	
124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
134	  intro T s
135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
137	
138	variable (C) in
139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
140	
141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
152	
153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
154	
155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
158	
159	variable (C) in
160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
161	
162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
165	
166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
186	
187	end
188	
189	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	
9	/-!
10	# C9b: the restricted chart map and the `(f, hf)` pair
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` builds the Abel chart map `abelSigmaChart` out of a
13	representation of the divisor functor, and its header states — correctly — that
14	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)` is **false as stated for the whole divisor
15	scheme**: the Abel map has projective spaces `|D|` as fibres, so it is not even a
16	monomorphism.  It becomes an open immersion only after restriction to the locus where the
17	fibre is a single point.
18	
19	This file supplies the restriction, which is the half of C9b that needs no new mathematics
20	once `chartLocus` exists — and it makes precise which half does.
21	
22	## What C9b consists of, and which part is here
23	
24	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) consumes a pair
25	`(f, hf)`.  Producing it from `abelSigmaChart` factors into exactly two steps:
26	
27	1. **restrict the source along an open immersion** — `restrictChart` below.  Given any open
28	   `V ⊆ D.left`, precomposing `abelSigmaChart` with `yoneda.map V.ι` gives a chart map out of
29	   `V`, and this is a *composition* of presheaf morphisms.  Landed here, sorry-free.
30	2. **certify the restricted map an open immersion of presheaves** — the honest content.
31	   `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` (mathlib `MorphismProperty.relative`) has two clauses:
32	   relative representability, and the open-immersion property of every represented pullback.
33	   Step 1 supplies the *left* factor of both clauses for free
34	   (`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map_of_isOpenImmersion` +
35	   `MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`), so what remains is exactly the
36	   corresponding statement for `abelSigmaChart` restricted to `V = chartLocus`, i.e.
37	   CHART-U(c): on the chart locus the Abel map is a bijection onto its image because the
38	   normalized effective representative is unique there (DAT-C GAP-2).
39	
40	So: the *composition* half of the `hf` certificate is discharged here, unconditionally; the
41	*chart-locus* half is CHART-U(c) and is stated but not proved (it needs GAP-2 plus the
42	classifier, and the openness of the locus itself, `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`).
43	
44	## CORRECTION 2026-07-29: step 2 above is itself TWO clauses, not one
45	
46	The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
47	wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
48	representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
49	represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
50	second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
51	unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.
52	
53	That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
54	elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
55	reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
56	*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
57	Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.
58	
59	## Main declarations
60	
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` — an open immersion of schemes is
62	  an open immersion of presheaves under yoneda.  This is mathlib's `relative_map` at
63	  `P := IsOpenImmersion`, recorded once with the instances it needs discharged.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.restrictChart` — the chart map restricted to an open of the source.
65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` — **the composition half of
66	  `hf`**: if the unrestricted chart map is an open immersion of presheaves, so is any
67	  restriction of it along an open immersion.  Unconditional in the restriction.
68	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartHom_restrictChart` — the structure morphism of a restricted chart
69	  is the restriction of the structure morphism, so the `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis of
70	  `JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited (being locally of finite type is local on the
71	  source).
72	-/
73	
74	set_option autoImplicit false
75	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
76	
77	universe u
78	
79	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
80	
81	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
84	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
85	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
86	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
87	
88	noncomputable section
89	
90	/-! ## An open immersion of schemes is one of presheaves -/
91	
92	/-- **Open immersions transfer through yoneda**: for an open immersion of schemes
93	`g : X ⟶ Y`, the induced map of yoneda presheaves satisfies `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`.
94	
95	This is mathlib's `MorphismProperty.relative_map` specialised to `F := yoneda` and
96	`P := @IsOpenImmersion`; the two side conditions it needs — that open immersions are stable
97	under base change, and that yoneda preserves the relevant pullbacks (it is fully faithful and
98	`Scheme` has pullbacks) — are discharged by instances.
99	
100	Recorded as a named lemma because it is the *only* source of `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
101	facts anywhere in this tree that does not go through a chart certificate: every restriction
102	of a chart map is built from it. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
104	    [IsOpenImmersion g] :
105	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map g) :=
106	  MorphismProperty.relative_map (P := @IsOpenImmersion) (F := yoneda) ‹IsOpenImmersion g›
107	
108	/-! ## The restricted chart map -/
109	
110	/-- **The chart map restricted to an open of its source.**
111	
112	`f` is the unrestricted chart map (in practice `abelSigmaChart`, whose source is the divisor
113	scheme) and `V` an open subscheme of the source; the restriction is the composition with the
114	yoneda image of the open inclusion.
115	
116	The point of restricting is that the unrestricted Abel map is *not* an open immersion of
117	presheaves — see the `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep` header — while its restriction to the locus where
118	the fibre is a single point is.  This definition is neutral about which open `V` is; the
119	chart-locus choice enters only in the certificate. -/
120	def restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
121	    (V : X.Opens) : yoneda.obj (V : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
122	  yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f
123	
124	/-- **The composition half of the `hf` certificate**: a restriction of an open immersion of
125	presheaves along an open immersion is again one.
126	
127	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is `MorphismProperty.relative` at `yoneda`, which is stable under
128	composition (`MorphismProperty.relative_isStableUnderComposition`, needing `yoneda` full and
129	faithful and `IsOpenImmersion` stable under composition — all instances).  Together with
130	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map` this discharges, for free and in full generality, the
131	part of C9b that is bookkeeping.
132	
133	What it does NOT discharge, and what is therefore the whole remaining content of C9b: the
134	hypothesis `hfV`.  For `f := abelSigmaChart` that hypothesis is FALSE for `V = ⊤` and is
135	expected to be true for `V = chartLocus` — it is CHART-U(c), whose proof needs the
136	uniqueness of the normalized effective representative (DAT-C GAP-2) and the classifier.  A
137	lane must not read this lemma as reducing C9b to plumbing; it isolates the plumbing so the
138	mathematics is visible. -/
139	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart {X : Scheme.{u}}
140	    {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : X.Opens)
141	    (hfV : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f) :
142	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart f V) :=
143	  MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition.comp_mem _ _
144	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_yoneda_map V.ι) hfV
145	
146	/-! ## CHART-U(c): the remaining obligation, pinned
147	
148	With the composition half discharged, `hf` for a restricted Abel chart reduces to a single
149	statement.  It is pinned here as a definition so that the gate has a name in Lean and not
150	only in a worksheet — the pattern `Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.IsChartDatumPresentation` uses.
151	
152	**Its field-level input is available.**  DAT-C GAP-2 (Σ-UNIQ-fld) is *landed*:
153	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`
154	(`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`) — for effective `D`, `D'` with equal Čech class
155	and `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`, `D' = D`.  (The `w4-datc` §0.3 GAP-2 row claimed no such lemma existed;
156	that claim was stale and is corrected there as of 2026-07-28.)  What CHART-U(c) still needs
157	beyond it is the *relative* statement — uniqueness in families over the locus — plus the
158	classifier `divRepClassifyZar`. -/
159	
160	variable (C π n) in
161	/-- **CHART-U(c), pinned**: the chart map is an open immersion of presheaves after restriction
162	to the locus where the fibre class has a unique effective representative.
163	
164	This is the whole remaining content of C9b's `hf`.  Stated as a `Prop`-valued definition
165	rather than proved, because its proof needs the *relative* form of GAP-2 over `chartLocus`
166	together with `divRepClassifyZar`; a lane that discharges it gets `hf` by feeding it to
167	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart`.
168	
169	Deliberately stated about `abelSigmaChart` and a *given* open `V`, rather than about
170	`chartLocus` directly: the openness of `chartLocus` is a separate obligation
171	(`Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen`), and keeping the two apart means neither has to wait for the
172	other. -/
173	def IsChartUniv {D : Over (Spec (.of k))} (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
174	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
176	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
177	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
178	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V)
179	
180	/-- The pinned obligation is exactly what `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart` would
181	give from an unrestricted certificate — recorded so that no lane proves the same thing
182	twice, and so that the *reason* the unrestricted route is unavailable stays visible: the
183	hypothesis of that lemma is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`. -/
184	lemma isChartUniv_of_unrestricted {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
186	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
187	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
188	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
189	    (V : D.left.Opens)
190	    (h : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :
191	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
192	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart V h
193	
194	/-! ## The structure morphism of a restricted chart -/
195	
196	/-- **The structure morphism of a restricted chart is the restriction of the structure
197	morphism.**  Hence the `LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom …)` hypothesis of
198	`JacobianData.ofCharts` is inherited by every restriction: being locally of finite type is
199	local on the source, and an open immersion is locally of finite type.
200	
201	Concretely, for the Abel chart of a representation `rep` by `D` the unrestricted structure

9	/-!
10	# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor
11	
12	This file constructs the **étale-sheafified relative Picard functor**
13	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}` of a smooth proper curve `C/k` and proves that it *is* a sheaf
14	for the étale topology — the object whose representability is the project's
15	central open obligation (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`).
16	
17	## Why the sheafification is the right object
18	
19	The relative Picard presheaf `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
20	(`Scheme.PicSharp.relPresheaf`, Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`) is in general **not
21	a sheaf**, not even for the Zariski topology (Kleiman §2, L1292–L1302): a line
22	bundle on `C ×_k T` can be trivial on each member of a cover of `T` without
23	being trivial modulo `π_T^* Pic(T)`, because the gluing data is a `Pic`-class
24	of the overlaps. Kleiman's representability theorem (§4 Thm. `th:main`) is
25	therefore a statement about the associated **étale** sheaf, and it is that
26	statement which is true over an arbitrary base field with no rational-point
27	hypothesis.
28	
29	There are two ways to reach a sheaf, and they differ in what has to be
30	supplied:
31	
32	1. assume `C` has a `k`-rational point. Then Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 says the
33	   comparison `Pic_{C/k} → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is already bijective, so the plain
34	   presheaf is the sheaf. This is *strictly weaker* than the challenge, whose
35	   curve need not have a rational point, and it is the route the conditional
36	   `Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` records;
37	2. sheafify. Nothing is assumed about `C(k)`, and the sheaf axiom holds by
38	   construction. This is the route realised here and the one the project
39	   claims (owner decision of 2026-07-28).
40	
41	## The site
42	
43	Mathlib `v4.31` carries the big étale site on schemes,
44	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleTopology = grothendieckTopology @Etale`
45	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`). The relative Picard presheaf
46	lives on the slice `Over (Spec k)` rather than on `Scheme`, so the topology is
47	transported along the localisation of SGA 4 III 5.2.1, available in Mathlib as
48	`GrothendieckTopology.over`: a sieve of `T : Over (Spec k)` covers iff the
49	corresponding sieve of `T.left` covers étale-locally. That transport is where
50	"the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`" becomes a definition rather than a parameter,
51	and it is what lets the sheaf property below be a *theorem* rather than a
52	hypothesis.
53	
54	## Main definitions
55	
56	* `Scheme.etaleTopologyOver k` — the étale topology on `(Sch/k) = Over (Spec k)`.
57	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` — `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, a bundled
58	  `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`, obtained by sheafifying the
59	  relative Picard presheaf.
60	* `Scheme.PicSharp.etaleSheaf_isSheaf` — the sheaf property, extracted as a
61	  standalone statement about the underlying presheaf.
62	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt C` — the set-valued functor
63	  `T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that the representability obligation is stated
64	  against, together with `picEtComparison C`, the canonical comparison
65	  `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` from the unsheafified functor.
66	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picEt_isSheaf_forget` — the sheaf property of `picEt`
67	  itself (the group structure forgotten), which is what a representing scheme
68	  must match.
69	
70	## References
71	
72	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Def. `df:Pfs` (the
73	étale-sheaf clause) and Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`), §4 Thm. `th:main`.
74	Blueprint: `def:rel_pic_etale_sheafification`,
75	`thm:rel_pic_etale_sheaf_group_structure`, `sec:fga_pic_setup`.
76	-/

83	
84	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

86	namespace Scheme

88	/-! ## §1. The étale site of `(Sch/k)` -/
89	
90	/-- **The étale topology on `(Sch/k)`.**
91	
92	The big étale topology on schemes (`Scheme.etaleTopology`, Mathlib
93	`AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean`) localised at `Spec k` along SGA 4
94	III 5.2.1 (`GrothendieckTopology.over`): a sieve of a `k`-scheme `T` is
95	covering exactly when the sieve it generates on the underlying scheme
96	`T.left` is covering for the étale topology
97	(`GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff`).
98	
99	This is the site on which the relative Picard presheaf of
100	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` lives, so it is the site whose sheafification
101	produces Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`. Note that the earlier
102	`PicSharp.etSheaf` of that file takes the topology as a *parameter*, for
103	want of a canonical choice; this definition supplies the canonical one, and
104	`PicSharp.etaleSheaf` below is the instantiation. -/
105	noncomputable abbrev etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
106	    GrothendieckTopology (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :=
107	  Scheme.etaleTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
108	
109	/-- The étale topology on `(Sch/k)` refines the Zariski one: a Zariski cover
110	of a `k`-scheme is an étale cover. Transported from
111	`zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology` through the localisation, which is
112	monotone because `mem_over_iff` characterises membership by the pushed-forward
113	sieve on the underlying scheme.
114	
115	Recorded because it is the precise sense in which sheafifying étale-locally is
116	*stronger* than sheafifying Zariski-locally: a Zariski sheaf need not be an
117	étale sheaf, and the relative Picard presheaf is not even the former. -/
118	theorem zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
119	    (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) ≤ etaleTopologyOver k := by
120	  intro T S hS
121	  rw [GrothendieckTopology.mem_over_iff] at hS ⊢
122	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology_le_etaleTopology _ hS
123	
124	namespace PicSharp
125	
126	/-! ## §2. The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor -/
127	
128	/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor** `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`
129	(Kleiman §2 Def. `df:Pfs`, étale-sheaf clause).
130	
131	The associated étale sheaf of the relative Picard presheaf
132	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` (`PicSharp.relPresheaf`), as a bundled object
133	of `Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat`. Its sheaf property is not an
134	assumption but part of the datum — `Sheaf.cond`, extracted as
135	`etaleSheaf_isSheaf` below — which is the whole point of passing to it: the
136	unsheafified `relPresheaf` is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally.
137	
138	This is a genuine instantiation of the parametric `PicSharp.etSheaf` of
139	`Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` at the canonical étale topology, with one
140	correction: `etSheaf` sheafifies the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`
141	(`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)`), whereas Kleiman's `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and the
142	representability theorem are about the *relative* one, `relPresheaf`. It is
143	the relative functor that is sheafified here.
144	
145	The abelian-group structure survives sheafification because the target
146	`AddCommGrpCat` has the sheafification adjunction
147	(`HasWeakSheafify` for a concrete, filtered-colimit-preserving forgetful
148	functor); `toEtaleSheaf` below is the unit. -/
149	noncomputable def etaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
150	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
151	    Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} :=
152	  (CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}).obj
153	    (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
154	
155	/-- **The sheaf property of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, as a standalone statement.**
156	
157	The underlying presheaf of `PicSharp.etaleSheaf C` satisfies the sheaf axiom
158	for the étale topology on `(Sch/k)`. This is `Sheaf.cond` of the bundled
159	object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
160	representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
161	represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
162	subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
163	exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).
164	
165	Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
166	theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
167	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
168	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
169	  (etaleSheaf C).property
170	
171	/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
172	sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.
173	
174	Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
175	`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
176	arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
177	which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
178	noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
179	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
180	    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
181	  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)
182	
183	/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
184	every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
185	of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.
186	
187	This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
188	sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
189	sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
190	noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
191	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
193	    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
194	    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
195	  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
196	    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)
197	
198	end PicSharp
199	
200	namespace PicScheme

202	/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/
203	
204	/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
205	the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
206	forgotten,
207	
208	```
209	picEt C : (Sch/k)^op ⥤ Type (u+1),   T ↦ Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T).
210	```
211	
212	Representability is a statement about the underlying set-valued functor; the
213	group structure is transported back onto the representing scheme by Yoneda
214	(`PicScheme.groupSchemeStructure`), exactly as for the unsheafified
215	`picSharp`.
216	
217	Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
218	representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
219	Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
220	Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
221	noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
222	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
223	    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
224	  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}
225	
226	/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
227	set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
228	`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.

230	The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as

11	
12	For the challenge curve `C` over `k`, an étale Picard class `λ : picEt C T` on an
13	arbitrary test object restricts along any field point `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` to a class
14	of the affine étale Picard group of `Spec K`, which collapses through the affine
15	comparison `picEtAffineEquiv` to a plus class in `PicEtAff C K` — whose degree
16	`PicEtAff.degAff` (SB-6) is an honest integer.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt λ t` — **the degree of an étale Picard class at a field
19	  point** (gap G-D6): the plus-class degree of the restriction of `λ` along `t`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_picEtMap` / `degAt_picEtFunctor_map` — functoriality: the
21	  degree of a restricted class at a field point is the degree of the original class at
22	  the composed field point.  Pure `picEtMap_comp` rewriting, which is what makes the
23	  degree-zero subfunctor stability definitional.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Subgroup C T` — the subgroup of classes of degree zero at
25	  *every* field point of `T` (membership: `mem_pic0Subgroup_iff`).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Functor C : (Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat` — **the
27	  degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
28	  subfunctor of `picEtFunctor C` cut out by the degree-zero condition, the binding
29	  carrier of the Wave-4 representability statement (`RepresentableBy`, design §2.7).

31	  (the naturality square of the inclusion, element form) and the bundled inclusion
32	  natural transformation `pic0Inclusion : pic0Functor C ⟶ picEtFunctor C`.

# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level

For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
which is the point of the vehicle.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
  of test algebras.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).

Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
-/

noncomputable section

/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/

namespace PicEtAff

variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom
  invFun := mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom
  left_inv x := by
    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k A from
      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a]
    exact mapAlg_id C x
  right_inv x := by
    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k B from
      AlgHom.ext fun b => e.apply_symm_apply b]
    exact mapAlg_id C x
  map_mul' x y := map_mul (mapAlg C e.toAlgHom) x y

@[simp]
lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C A) :
    congr C e x = mapAlg C e.toAlgHom x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C B) :
    (congr C e).symm x = mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom x :=
  rfl

end PicEtAff

/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/

variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))

/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
def picEtSubgroup :
    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]

/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
def picEt : Type u :=
  picEtSubgroup C T

noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))

/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/

  s.2 U V h

  Subtype.ext (funext h)

  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp

/-!
# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests

For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
refinement.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
  `h` of covers.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
  algebra.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
  descent datum.

The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
-/

# Zariski descent of representability (`thm:representability_zariski_descent`)

This file proves **Zariski descent of representability** (EGA 0_I 4.5.4;
cf. Stacks 01JJ): a presheaf `F : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type 1` satisfying the Zariski
sheaf axiom (`Scheme.IsZariskiSheafOver`, stated against open covers of the
total space of each `T : Over S`) that is representable over every member of
an open cover of `S` is representable by an `S`-scheme
(`Scheme.representable_of_openCover`).

The definitions `overRes` / `overResHom` / `overResLE` / `IsZariskiSheafOver`
and the statement of the descent theorem previously lived in
`GrassmannianRepresentability.lean` (where the theorem was a typed `sorry`
leaf); they are moved here so the Grassmannian file can consume the proof.

## Proof architecture

The heavy gluing content (cocycle conditions, `Scheme.GlueData`, the
locally-bijective sheaf comparison) is **not** redone by hand: it is delegated
to mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy`
(Stacks 01JJ), which applies to a `Type 0`-valued Zariski *sheaf* on the
absolute category `Scheme.{0}` equipped with a jointly surjective family of
relatively representable open immersions from representables.  The work done
here is the translation layer:

1. **Size reduction / total functor** (`ZariskiDescent.GluedPoint`,
   `ZariskiDescent.gluedFunctor`): the values of `F` live in `Type 1`, so `F`
   cannot be fed to the mathlib theorem directly.  Instead we encode a point
   of the would-be total space over `T : Scheme` as a `Type 0` datum: a base
   morphism `a : T ⟶ S` together with a family of *classifying morphisms*
   `γ i : T|_{a⁻¹ U i} ⟶ Y i` into the local representing objects, compatible
   on overlaps as classified `F`-sections.  The bespoke sheaf axiom for `F`
   shows `GluedPoint T ≃ Σ (a : T ⟶ S), F(T, a)` (`ZariskiDescent.totalEquiv`),
   identifying `gluedFunctor` with the (large) total functor of `F`.
2. **Sheaf axiom** (`ZariskiDescent.isSheaf`): `gluedFunctor` is a sheaf for
   the big Zariski topology.  Covers by arbitrary jointly surjective open
   immersions are reduced to covers by opens of the target (the generated
   sieves agree), where the claim follows from the sheaf axiom of `F` through
   `totalEquiv`.
3. **Charts** (`ZariskiDescent.chart`): each `Y i` maps to `gluedFunctor` by
   sending `t : T ⟶ (Y i).left` to the point classified by the `F`-section
   that `t` represents; these are relatively representable open immersions
   (the pullback against a point `(a, x)` of `gluedFunctor` is the open
   subscheme `a⁻¹ U i ⊆ T`) and jointly surjective.
4. **Conclusion**: mathlib glues a scheme `Ŷ` with `gluedFunctor ≅ Hom(-, Ŷ)`;
   the tautological point of `Ŷ` gives the structure morphism `â : Ŷ ⟶ S`,
   and `totalEquiv` converts the absolute representability into
   `F.RepresentableBy (Over.mk â)`.
